# Overview {.unnumbered}

This is a note I wrote several years ago. I was trying to introduce pencils of conics and their isoconjugations, but found this too complicated over the real projective plane, so I instead made another note on the complex projective plane. That means, I am unlikely to update this note in the future.

Since this was intended to be a note, I didn't give a title to each section until this whole note was finished. These titles are just a suggestion of what would probably be in that section.

The following translation is AI-generated.

# Notations {.unnumbered}

Unless otherwise stated, $\triangle ABC$ is taken as the reference triangle.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false}
## Notations throughout the note

* Let $\ell_1\cap \ell_2$ denote the intersection of lines $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$.

* Let $(XYZ)$ denote the circumcircle of $XYZ$, and let $(XY)$ denote the circle of diameter $XY$.

* Let $X_{\perp \ell}$ denote the foot of the perpendicular from $X$ to line $\ell$.

* Let $M_{XY}$ denote the midpoint of $XY$.

* We use $\measuredangle$ for directed angles.

* The power of a point $X$ with respect to a circle $\omega$ is denoted by $\mathrm{Pow}_\omega(X)$.

* Let $\ell_\infty$ denote the line at infinity.

* Let $\infty_\ell$ denote the point of infinity on $\ell$, and let $\infty_{\perp \ell}$ denote the point at infinity in the direction perpendicular to $\ell$.

* Let $\mathbb{L}_X$ denote the pencil of lines through $X$.

* The cross ratio of four points is denoted by $(X_1,X_2;X_3,X_4)$.

* We use $\mathfrak{p}_{\mathcal{C}}$ for the polar transform.

* Let $\mathcal{T}_\mathcal{C}$ denote the envelope of the conic $\mathcal{C}$.

* Let $I$ denote the incenter of $ABC$, and let $I_A,I_B,I_C$ denote the $A,B,C$-excenters, respectively.

* Let $O,H,G,N_9$ denote the circumcenter, orthocenter, centroid, and nine-point center of $ABC$, respectively.

* Let $Ge,Na,Sp,Be$ denote the Gergonne point, Nagel point, Spieker center, and Bevan point of $ABC$, respectively.

* Let $K,Br,Br'$ denote the symmedian point and the two Brocard points of $ABC$, respectively.

* Let $\mathcal{H}_{Fe}$ denote the Feuerbach hyperbola, and let $Mt,Sc, Fe$ denote the Mittenpunkt, Schiffler point, and Feuerbach point of $ABC$, respectively.

* Let $\mathcal{K}$ denote the Kiepert hyperbola, and let $K_\theta\in\mathcal{K}$ be the standard parametrization.

* Let $\mathcal{H}_{Je}$ denote the Jerabek hyperbola, and let $Ko$ denote the Kosnita point of $ABC$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false}
## List of triangle centers

Let $X(n)$ denote the $n$-th triangle center.

* $X(1)$ is the incenter (the center of the incircle).

* $X(2)$ is the centroid (the concurrency point of the three medians).

* $X(3)$ is the circumcenter (the center of the circumcircle).

* $X(4)$ is the orthocenter (the concurrency point of the three altitudes).

* $X(5)$ is the nine-point center (the center of the nine-point circle).

* $X(6)$ is the symmedian point (the concurrency point of the three symmedians).

* $X(7)$ is the Gergonne point (the perspector of $ABC$ and the contact triangle).

* $X(8)$ is the Nagel point (the isotomic conjugate of $X(7)$).

* $X(9)$ is the Mittenpunkt (the symmedian point of the excentral triangle).

* $X(10)$ is the Spieker center (the incenter of the medial triangle).

* $X(11)$ is the Feuerbach point.

* $X(12)$ is the insimilicenter of the incircle and the nine-point circle.

* $X(13)$ is the first isogonic center (the point $K_{60^\circ}$ on the Kiepert hyperbola).

* $X(14)$ is the second isogonic center (the point $K_{-60^\circ}$ on the Kiepert hyperbola).

* $X(15)$ is the first isodynamic point (the isogonal conjugate of $X(13)$).

* $X(16)$ is the second isodynamic point (the isogonal conjugate of $X(14)$).

* $X(17)$ is the first Napoleon point (the point $K_{30^\circ}$ on the Kiepert hyperbola).

* $X(18)$ is the second Napoleon point (the point $K_{-30^\circ}$ on the Kiepert hyperbola).

* $X(20)$ is the deLong Champs point (the anticomplement of $X(4)$).

* $X(21)$ is the Schiffler point (second intersection of the Euler line and the Feuerbach hyperbola).

* $X(25)$ is the homothety center of the orthic triangle and the tangential triangle.

* $X(26)$ is the circumcenter of the tangential triangle.

* $X(30)$ is the point of infinity on the Euler line.

* $X(36)$ is the inverse of $X(1)$ with respect to the circumcircle.

* $X(40)$ is the Bevan point (the reflection of $X(1)$ across $X(3)$).

* $X(54)$ is the Kosnita point (the isogonal conjugate of $X(5)$).

* $X(55)$ is the insimilicenter of the circumcircle and the incircle.

* $X(56)$ is the exsimilicenter of the circumcircle and the incircle.

* $X(57)$ is the homothety center of the excentral triangle and the contact triangle.

* $X(61)$ is the isogonal conjugate of $X(17)$.

* $X(62)$ is the isogonal conjugate of $X(18)$.

* $X(64)$ is the isogonal conjugate of $X(20)$.

* $X(65)$ is the orthocenter of the contact triangle.

* $X(69)$ is the isotomic conjugate of $X(4)$.

* $X(74)$ is the fourth intersection of the Jerabek hyperbola and the circumcircle.

* $X(79)$ is the concurrency point of $ABC$ and the triangle formed by the reflection of $X(1)$ over the three sides.

* $X(80)$ is the antigonal conjugate of $X(1)$.

* $X(84)$ is the isogonal conjugate of $X(40)$.

* $X(104)$ is the second intersection of the Feuerbach hyperbola and the circumcircle.

* $X(110)$ is the antipode of $X(74)$ on the circumcircle.

* $X(115)$ is the center of the Kiepert hyperbola.

* $X(125)$ is the center of the Jerabek hyperbola.

* $X(182)$ ia the midpoint of $X(3)X(6)$.
:::
